"""Starting architecture: the main campaign's default policy (conv encoder, width 64, depth 2, ReLU,
no normalisation), rewritten as a candidate file. A 3x3 conv body, a 1x1 conv placement head
(one logit per brick type and anchor cell), and DONE and value heads on mean+max pooled features."""
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

WIDTH = 64
DEPTH = 2


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        layers, c_in = [], spec.in_channels
        for _ in range(DEPTH):
            layers += [nn.Conv2d(c_in, WIDTH, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU()]
            c_in = WIDTH
        self.body = nn.Sequential(*layers)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(WIDTH, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * WIDTH, WIDTH), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(WIDTH, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting recipe's four seeds split into three runs at 0.068 and one at 0.258, so seed noise is large and only differences of several points mean anything. The default recipe also does very few updates: 131,072 steps divided by 4,096 per update gives only 32 policy iterations. Three things in the recipe may be limiting learning: (1) data, since fewer PPO epochs buy more samples (1 epoch gives about 3.25 times as many steps); (2) policy iterations, since smaller rollout batches give more updates at the same budget; (3) credit assignment, since the +1 exact-build bonus comes at the end of episodes that can last up to 41 steps, and gamma 0.95 discounts it heavily. I test each idea on its own to see which one moves dev success.
analyses.2: All five round-1 seeds ended at exactly 0.0684 (35/512) or very close to it. The starting recipe had one seed reach 0.258. So the agent reliably gets stuck at the same point, and only a lucky seed gets past it. Three changes did not move that plateau at all: one PPO epoch (3x more samples), a longer horizon, and more policy updates. Seeds that land on the identical score point to a fixed local optimum, not undertraining. The likely cause is that the policy settles early on a habit, such as never pressing DONE at the right moment or a fixed placement routine, that only solves the easiest designs. Exploration and update size have not been tested yet, so this round tests them. Each candidate keeps ppo_epochs=1 (the r1c1 base, which gives the most samples). One adds more entropy. Two bracket the learning rate, one lower and one higher, to see whether the plateau comes from the policy settling too early or from it learning too slowly.
analyses.3: Every recipe so far gives exactly 0.0684 on both seeds: 1 epoch, high or low lr, more entropy, a longer gamma, and more updates. 0.0684 is 35 of the 512 dev designs. Training success sits at about 0.065. This looks like a stable local optimum: probably a greedy fill that only works on easy designs. Changing update size, sample count or entropy does not move it. Only one of the starting architecture's default-recipe seeds got past it (0.258), so getting past it is rare luck. Choices not yet tested: rollouts long enough to hold whole episodes (up to 41 placements) so the +1 exact-build bonus is not lost to a weak critic's bootstrap, very aggressive reuse of each sample (8 epochs, wider clip), and no entropy bonus over the roughly 400 actions. All three are new directions, because fine changes around the current best have only reproduced the same plateau.
analyses.4: Of the nine trials, eight finished at about 0.068 on both seeds (0.0674 to 0.0684). Neither seed of those runs escaped the plateau. That includes 1 epoch with more samples, higher or lower learning rate, more entropy, no entropy, longer gamma, full-episode rollouts and more updates at 4 epochs. Fresh samples and exploration settings do not seem to be the bottleneck. The only trial to beat the plateau on both seeds was r3c2: 8 epochs, clip 0.3 and 2,048-sample updates, scoring 0.117 and 0.154 (mean 0.136). Its mean is above the start's 4-seed mean of 0.116, but with two seeds and this much noise that is weak evidence. Heavy reuse of each sample is the one lever that has helped.
